reviewNotes: Rebuilt on 2026-10-17 with profile ci (opt-level 3, LTO disabled, codegen-units 16; not a fat-LTO release validation) in the pinned official rust:1.99.0-trixie image (index SHA-256 81015672d6939b0265f09adf96d5de125482bb1330106076956b0518e74edc90) with Debian 13 packages from snapshot 20261016T180000Z. dpkg evidence confirms gcc-mingw-w64-x86-64-win32 14.2.0-19+27+b1 (win32 thread model) and mingw-w64-x86-64-dev 12.0.0-5. The linker map links crt2.o, crtbegin.o/crtend.o, libmingw32/libmingwex runtime members, system import stubs, libgcc _ctors.o and libgcc_eh unwind-seh.o, now from the GCC 14 directory; no winpthreads member is present, and the fourteen reviewed native paths and eleven system DLL imports are otherwise unchanged from the Bookworm review. The Rust 1.99.0 standard-library aggregate and its twelve standalone sysroot texts are unchanged; preserve that complete aggregate and every notice/exception; compiler implementation dependencies remain outside the inventory. Reviewed the changed Debian copyright files verbatim: mingw-w64 12.0.0's adds header and IDL stanzas (LGPL-2.1+, expat, NCSA-LLVM) and reorganizes file lists, while the linked CRT and runtime objects keep their ZPL-2.1 and public-domain terms; gcc-mingw-w64's differs only in its packaging copyright year; GPL-3 is identical. libbcrypt.a is now SHA-256 db754b1ec02453061ba6e9fac313f07e30f43c128803c864ccfde255c731bd58; BCryptGenRandom remains an import trampoline to bcrypt.dll, covered by the mingw-w64 ZPL-2.1 attribution. The SystemFunction036 fallback uses ADVAPI32.dll. Retain the mingw-w64 copyright/ZPL-2.1 terms and disclaimer, and the GCC GPLv3 notices with GCC Runtime Library Exception 3.1 for linked libgcc objects. Windows system DLLs are not bundled. Distributed builds check the native/import closure against this allowlist and check the actual notice text fingerprint. Binary hashes and full compiler version strings are not legal approval inputs; the pinned builder and toolchain establish their provenance.
description: Rust 1.99.0 standard-library notices and Debian Trixie mingw-w64 runtime/startup attribution for Windows. mingw-w64 startup/runtime/import-library objects and GCC runtime objects are statically linked; Windows system DLLs are not bundled. Native paths and notices are reviewed for the x86_64-w64-mingw32 cross inputs of the pinned official Rust Trixie builder.

reviewNotes: Hosted CI run 37112635227 at commit 1a68553b generated the actual native linker maps and canonical input listings using the pinned official rust:1.99.0-bookworm image (index SHA-256 59037199c44290f2befcdd58dcc540164763fc296950255aaefeef096a1866b0). The probe used profile ci: opt-level 3, LTO disabled, codegen-units 16; it was not a fat-LTO release validation. The historical complete input listings match their original candidate fingerprints. The notice-only fingerprint was derived from those verified listings and retains every actual standard-library and additional notice text; the exported standard-library bytes were rechecked against their listed hashes. Reviewed the complete Rust 1.99.0 standard-library aggregate and all twelve standalone sysroot license texts. The standalone texts, in-tree notices and retained component notice bodies are unchanged from 1.98.1; dependency versions changed without new license expressions, and libc author metadata changed in the upstream aggregate. Preserve that complete aggregate and every notice/exception; compiler implementation dependencies remain outside the inventory. The x86_64 server and TUI canonical listings and actual native path sets are identical. Their maps link rcrt1.o, crti.o/crtn.o, crtbeginS.o/crtendS.o, libc.a and libunwind.a, with no imported system library; no GCC startup/runtime object is linked from the Debian driver. Rust 1.99.0 src/ci/docker/scripts/musl.sh pins musl 1.2.5 with the CVE-2025-26519, CVE-2026-6042 and CVE-2026-40200 patches; hosted native .comment evidence reports GCC 9.4.0. LLVM libunwind and compiler-rt startup source provenance is Rust 1.99.0's src/llvm-project submodule 1b9c0d5ff9bbe7634aead059efe6b11a7eeba145. Its exact libunwind/compiler-rt LICENSE.TXT bytes were inspected and remain identical to the existing Apache-2.0 WITH LLVM-exception notices; rust-notice-sources.json pins their new source commit and unchanged hashes, together with the musl MIT copyright. Preserve all these notices. The probe observed the startup selection after Rust 1.99's static-PIE support change; distributed builds validate their native/import closure and notice text fingerprint. Binary hashes and full compiler version strings are not legal approval inputs; the pinned builder and toolchain establish their provenance. External musl/LLVM notice sources are bound to the pinned Rust version in rust-notice-sources.json, so toolchain upgrades require their source review even when paths and legal text bytes stay unchanged. Rebuilt on 2026-10-17 with profile ci in the pinned rust:1.99.0-trixie builder (index SHA-256 81015672d6939b0265f09adf96d5de125482bb1330106076956b0518e74edc90, Debian 13 snapshot 20261016T180000Z): the linked native paths, the absence of imported system libraries and the notice fingerprint are unchanged; C dependencies compiled with the Debian 13 cross compilers and musl 1.2.5-3.1~deb13u1 headers add Debian GCC 14.2.0 .comment evidence only.
description: Rust 1.99.0 standard-library, musl libc 1.2.5 and LLVM runtime notices for the static x86_64-unknown-linux-musl TUI and server. Rust's self-contained startup objects, libc.a and LLVM libunwind are linked; no system library is imported. Native paths and notices are reviewed for the rustup target archives in the pinned official Rust Trixie builder.
